name: Zakopane and the Tatras
tagline: Poland's alpine capital, a town of carved wooden villas at the foot of jagged peaks, with turquoise lakes, cable cars and highland cheese.
highlight: Morskie Oko, a glacial lake ringed by granite peaks, reached by an easy walk from the road.
shortDescription: The gateway to the Polish Tatras, with the carved-wood Zakopane style, Morskie Oko lake, the Kasprowy Wierch cable car, Giewont, hiking, skiing and smoked oscypek cheese.
metaDescription: A Zakopane and Tatras travel guide: Morskie Oko, Giewont, Kasprowy Wierch, Krupówki street, wooden architecture, hiking, skiing, oscypek cheese, where to stay, how to get there and a two-day plan.
knownFor: Tatra Mountains, Morskie Oko, wooden architecture, skiing

image.alt: The lake Morskie Oko with the Tatra peaks reflected in its water

intro: The Tatras are the highest mountain range in the Carpathians and the only truly alpine range in Poland, forming a natural border with Slovakia. Jagged granite peaks rise to 2,499 metres at Rysy, above deep valleys, glacial lakes and pine forests, and most of the Polish side is a national park. Zakopane, at the foot, is the region's unofficial capital.

The town has its own architecture and culture. In the late 19th century, artists developed the Zakopane Style, a fanciful wooden architecture with carved gables that is visible in villas and churches such as the small chapel at Jaszczurówka. The highland (górale) people have their own music, costumes and food, above all oscypek, a smoked sheep's cheese grilled and served with cranberry jam. Krupówki, the main pedestrian street, is a busy line of shops and restaurants.

In summer, people come to hike: the trail to Morskie Oko, Poland's most famous lake, is a wide road that is easy for families, and harder routes climb to Giewont, with its cross, or to the ridge. A cable car goes up to Kasprowy Wierch for high views, and in winter Zakopane is Poland's ski capital. Two or three days is a good stay.

whyVisit.intro: Zakopane is Poland's mountain playground, with scenery and a distinct highland culture.

attractionsIntro: The town is the base, and the mountains are a short bus ride away.

attractions.name: Morskie Oko

image.alt: Morskie Oko lake in the early morning light

attractions.text: A glacial lake at 1,395 metres, ringed by peaks, reached by a 9-km road walk from Palenica Białczańska.
attractions.tip: Go early, since the road gets crowded.

attractions.name: Giewont

image.alt: The Giewont mountain, known as the Sleeping Knight, above Zakopane

attractions.text: A mountain topped with a steel cross whose profile looks like a sleeping knight, reached by a demanding hike.
attractions.tip: Avoid storms; the summit is exposed.

attractions.name: Krupówki Street

image.alt: The pedestrian street Krupówki in Zakopane lined with shops

attractions.text: The main pedestrian street, lined with shops, restaurants and stalls selling oscypek and highland goods.

attractions.name: Jaszczurówka Chapel

image.alt: The wooden Jaszczurówka chapel in the Zakopane Style

attractions.text: A small wooden chapel of 1907 that is a masterpiece of the Zakopane Style.

attractions.name: Kasprowy Wierch
attractions.text: A cable car to a 1,987-metre summit on the Slovak border, with big views.

attractions.name: Rysy

image.alt: The peak of Rysy in the High Tatras

attractions.text: Poland's highest peak at 2,499 metres, a serious hike for experienced walkers.
attractions.tip: Only in summer, with good weather.

thingsToDoIntro: Zakopane is for hiking and highland culture.

thingsToDo.title: Walk to Morskie Oko
thingsToDo.text: An easy road walk to a famous lake.

foodIntro: Highland food is smoky and hearty.

gettingThere.intro: Zakopane is reached by bus or minibus from Kraków.

options.text: About 2 hours, with heavy traffic in peak times.

gettingAround.intro: Buses and minibuses cover the area.

bestTime.headline: June–September and December–March
bestTime.summary: Summer suits hikers and winter suits skiers.
bestTime.avoid: November and April, when trails are icy or wet.

itinerary.intro: A lake day and a town day.
